meaning: The service that holds the waiting jobs, starts machines for them and removes the machines when the work is done.

The way you buy cloud machines: On-Demand, Spot Instances, Savings Plans, Capacity Blocks for ML or On-Demand Capacity Reservations. Some purchase options let AWS reclaim a machine in the middle of a job, and others do not.
The saved weights of a policy, or the saved state of a job from which the job can resume.
One AWS Batch submission that creates between 2 and 10,000 child jobs. Each child reads its own index number and uses it to pick its piece of work.
The layer that holds the waiting jobs and decides which one runs next.
The layer that starts a machine when a job is waiting and removes it when no job is waiting.
A managed job queue for containers. It starts EC2 instances for waiting jobs and removes them when the queue is empty.
The component of AWS Batch that starts the instances for the jobs in a job queue.
The AWS service that rents virtual machines, which AWS calls instances.
Managed Slurm. AWS runs the Slurm controller, and compute node groups launch EC2 instances for waiting jobs.
In AWS PCS, the group of EC2 instances that PCS launches for waiting jobs. Each group has exactly one purchase option.
A job scheduler that comes from supercomputing. You submit work to it with commands such as sbatch.
A persistent cluster of GPU instances that AWS keeps healthy by replacing failed nodes. You schedule work on it with Slurm or with Kubernetes.
A managed run of one training container. It bills for the duration of the job and then shuts the instances down.
Managed Kubernetes. AWS runs the control plane, and you add the parts that start nodes and queue jobs.
An open-source node provisioner for Kubernetes. It starts EC2 instances for pods that fit on no existing node.
A managed form of Karpenter-based scaling, in which AWS also runs the node software.
A Kubernetes add-on that holds jobs against per-team quotas and decides when each job can start.
An open-source Kubernetes scheduler with queues and quotas for GPU work.
A Kubernetes object that manages several Jobs as one unit and restarts them together.
The EC2 network device that lets the nodes of one job exchange data without going through the operating system's network stack.
An EC2 setting that keeps the nodes of one job physically close together.
The purchase option with no commitment. AWS makes no promise that an instance is available when you ask for one.
Spare EC2 capacity sold at a discount. EC2 can reclaim a Spot Instance in the middle of a job.
The event in which EC2 reclaims a Spot Instance. EC2 announces it two minutes before, on a best-effort basis.
An EC2 signal that a Spot Instance is at elevated risk of interruption.
Capacity held for one instance type in one Availability Zone for as long as you keep it. You pay the On-Demand rate whether or not an instance runs in it.
A reservation of GPU instances for a fixed period, booked in advance and paid up front.
A capacity reservation made through SageMaker for a HyperPod cluster or a training job.
A discount on the bill for the instances an account runs.
AWS's own training chip, sold as the trn instance types.
EC2 GPU instances whose GPUs have ray-tracing cores. They are used for rendering and simulation.
EC2 GPU instances whose GPUs are sized for training throughput.
The AWS event bus. It routes events, such as a new S3 object or a Spot interruption notice, to the targets you choose.
The AWS workflow service. It runs the steps of a workflow as states, and one state can submit an AWS Batch job and wait for it to finish.
NVIDIA's open-source workflow orchestrator for physical AI pipelines. It runs on Kubernetes clusters.
An experiment tracking server and model registry. SageMaker offers it as a managed service.
A client that presents an S3 bucket as a local file system. It can read files and create new ones, but it cannot modify existing files.
A managed shared file system with full POSIX file-system behaviour.
The remote-desktop protocol for interactive workstations on EC2.
Software on a device that receives versioned components from the cloud and runs them.
A software package that AWS IoT Greengrass receives from the cloud and runs on the device. Its recipe names its dependencies and the commands that install and run it.
A feature that attaches a machine outside AWS to an EKS cluster as a node.
